doc: References over the Hierarchical Requirement Designer's binding, hierarchical-requirement.fbl#markdown (User Story 6; FR-041, FR-043, FR-044, SC-003). A reference is a mention (DESL 0.2 section 4.3): the facet mentions of an item's and a requirement's description and of an assessment's about, text and detail in hierarchical-requirement.des, whose pattern \[(?:ITEM|REQ)-\d+\]\([^)]*\)|\[(?<id>(?:ITEM|REQ)-\d+)\] reads [REQ-0002] as a mention and a link with a target as none. The binding gives no slot a reference (FBL section 5.7), so FBL reads and writes every one of them as text. Reading the input: the mentions on line 8 (ITEM-0001's description), line 12 (REQ-0002's description), line 20 (an assessment about REQ-0002, whose text mentions REQ-0003) and lines 21 and 22 (an assessment about ITEM-0002, whose detail mentions REQ-0002 and ITEM-0003) all name an entry, while REQ-0001's title (line 9) and the link on line 10 both write [REQ-0099], which no entry has: a title carries no mentions facet and the link is no mention, so read lists no finding. The document attributes lastItem ITEM-0003 and lastRequirement REQ-0004 come from line 2 and are not elements. The steps, each followed by its undo so that each starts from the input: a description set with [REQ-0002] in it on an entry without one and on one with one, the referred requirement REQ-0002 moved to another depth with every reference to it, and the one in its own description, left as written, and REQ-0002 deleted with every reference to it kept; deleted/ reads the document after the delete, with its three std.mentions findings. The file has CRLF endings.

steps.doc: setDescription on REQ-0003, which has no continuation, with a reference that the lookup wrote when the person typed # and picked REQ-0002 (FR-040, FR-041): an insert-key at the end of its item line, the value's line written after the line ending of that line, CRLF, and indented with spaces to REQ-0003's content column 6 (FBL 0.7 section 6.3, bullets, the continuation). The reference is written as the text [REQ-0002] and nothing else: FBL writes the value as it is given.

steps.doc: moveRequirement on REQ-0002 into ITEM-0002, which holds REQ-0003 only, so after REQ-0003 (hierarchical-requirement.des, moveRequirement: a move to another item after its last requirement), planned as FBL's move (DESL 0.2 section 8.2): a remove-entry of REQ-0002's line span, its item line and its continuation, and an insert-entry after the line span of REQ-0003, its previous sibling there, of the same bytes with every line that is not blank shifted right by 2, the difference between the column 4 a new item's marker has there (REQ-0003's) and the column 2 its marker had (FBL 0.7 sections 5.5 and 6.3, a move to another depth). Its number does not change (FR-011), and no reference is rewritten: the mentions on lines 8, 20 and 22 that name REQ-0002 and the one in its own description that names REQ-0001 are text, and the binding has no reference to rewrite (FBL section 5.7), so each names the same entry as before (SC-003). The edit has no rewrite-reference splice.

steps.doc: Its confirmation's count is 3: the assessment about REQ-0002, ITEM-0001's description and the detail that mentions it (hierarchical-requirement.des, deleteEntry), so the person is asked first. The delete is one remove-entry of REQ-0002's line span, which takes its continuation with it (FBL 0.7 sections 4.8 and 6.2); the rule's remove has no cascade. Nothing else is written: a mention is text, which no runtime changes when the element it names is deleted (DESL 0.2 section 4.3), so [REQ-0002] on line 8, the assessment about REQ-0002 and [REQ-0002] in the other assessment's detail are kept as written (FR-044), and the mark line keeps REQ-0004, so the number is not given again. deleted/ reads the result and lists the three std.mentions findings.
Undo puts back exactly the bytes the edit replaced: REQ-0002 and its description stand where they stood, and every mention of it names it again.
